options: Low calorie intake with high activity

questions.stem: In obese patients, how do airway complications compare with the general population, per NAP4?

options: A weak predictor on its own
Not related to airway difficulty at all

questions.stem: Beyond anatomy, what makes the obese airway physiologically difficult?
questions.answer: Reduced FRC, higher metabolic rate, aspiration risk

questions.stem: In obesity, what happens to FRC and lung compliance, and what does this lead to?
questions.answer: FRC and compliance fall, work of breathing rises, causing atelectasis and faster desaturation

questions.stem: Why does obesity cause faster desaturation and CO2 retention?
questions.answer: Higher O2 consumption and CO2 production from metabolically active fat

questions.answer: They gradually become insensitive to PaCO2

questions.stem: What three features make up the obesity hypoventilation syndrome triad?
questions.answer: Obesity (BMI >30), daytime hypercapnia (PaCO2 ≥45 mmHg), sleep-disordered breathing

questions.stem: What share of people with obstructive sleep apnoea are also obese?
What share of obese people have obstructive sleep apnoea?
What share of patients with obesity hypoventilation syndrome have OSA?
What share of patients with obesity hypoventilation syndrome have severe OSA?
Why do blood volume, MAP and cardiac output rise in obesity?
questions.answer: To meet the metabolic demand of fat

questions.answer: Raised intra-abdominal pressure, larger gastric volumes, delayed gastric emptying

questions.stem: Which three conditions should be optimised before surgery in obese patients?
questions.answer: BP, diabetes, and left or right heart failure

questions.answer: To prevent sores and nerve injury

questions.stem: In obesity, if the patient can walk, how can induction reduce manual handling?
questions.answer: They walk in, position on the table and are induced there

questions.stem: In obesity, what is needed to move the patient after surgery?

questions.answer: Difficult intubation, bag-mask ventilation and FONA; apnoea intolerance; aspiration
